title: Graceful Spillover Controller — SLO-driven regional routing & capacity-aware shedding
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Problem: During transient regional capacity crunches we observe cascading latency spikes and opaque failures for customers. Current pin/hedge heuristics are brittle: hard thresholds either over-evacuate traffic (increasing global cost) or under-protect local SLOs (raising p99).

Goal: Implement a Graceful Spillover Controller (GSC) that harmonizes regional SLOs with capacity signals to: 1) maintain per-region latency SLOs where possible, 2) gracefully spill traffic to compatible regions when necessary, 3) apply probabilistic, QoS-aware shedding and multi-tier circuit breakers to protect global health, and 4) provide observability and deterministic rollout knobs for operators.

Scope: Design and implement the routing policy component of GSC in the request director (control-plane decision service). This ticket covers policy logic, SLO scoring, regional capacity weighting, staged shedding schedules, and the control hooks to the runtime for enforcement. Implementation of new runtime token-shedding primitives is tracked as ENG-904777 (dependency). Excludes UI/Console work (separate PM ticket).
design_decisions: Use a rolling 5m window for primary SLO signal (p50/p90/p99 latency and availability), combined with 1m capacity heartbeat for rapid reaction.
SLO score: compute per-region = weighted sum(availability:40%, p99 latency:50%, error-rate:10%). Regions with score below a configurable threshold are candidates for spillover.
Probabilistic shedding tiers: soft (5-15%), medium (15-40%), hard (40-100%) — driven by severity and customer tier mapping.

Implement three circuit levels: local soft-circuit ( shed low-priority tokens ), regional breaker (divert non-pinned traffic), global backstop (redirect to lowest-latency compatible model variant or return controlled 503 with Retry-After).
Geo-pinning respects customer pins (explicit region) and soft-pinning uses affinity scores; soft-pinned requests are eligible for spillover only when local SLOs fall below emergency threshold.
Fallback routing prefers region with compatible model variant and available KV cache warmness score to reduce cold-start latency.
Expose all thresholds and weightings via config flags and runtime feature gates for staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: GSC service computes per-region SLO score and publishes it to the routing decision API every 30s.
Routing decision API returns deterministic decision for a given request context (region, customer tier, pin flag) and current SLO scores.

During injected failure scenario (see test plan), at least 95% of Tier-1 customers in non-impacted regions maintain p99 latency below target while overall global requests degrade gracefully with controlled shedding.
Circuit breaker transitions (soft->medium->hard) are observable in Grafana and emit structured events to the audit log with correlating tokens and reasons.
A canary rollout (5% traffic) shows no increase in error-rate for pinned customers and produces expected spillover traffic patterns in the dashboard.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit & integration tests in staging; simulation harness against synthetic traffic (latency spikes, capacity loss).
Phase 1: Deploy GSC in decision-plane read-only mode (observe-only) for 24h to validate scoring and decisions match simulation expectations.
Phase 2: Enable enforcement for 5% canary traffic targeting non-critical customers during low-traffic window (US morning). Monitor 30m burn-in.
Phase 3: Gradually increase to 25% then 50% over 72h with rollback window and operator-controlled thresholds.
Phase 4: Global enable with fast rollback runbook and emergency flag to turn on global backstop.
telemetry_and_alerts: New Grafana panel: per-region SLO score (time-series) + spillover rate + shed rate (by tier).
Create Alert: region_slo_score < emergency_threshold for 3 consecutive 30s windows -> SEV2 paging with runbook link.
Create Alert: spillover_rate > 10% for more than 2m -> Ops slack #regional-routing and auto-tag incident on dashboard.
Audit events for every circuit state change sent to centralized event-log (include reason, affected tokens, decision-id).
testing_plan: Unit tests for SLO score computation covering edge cases (zeros, NaNs, missing heartbeats).
Integration test: decision API + runtime enforcement in k8s cluster using traffic-driver (100k qps) with injected regional CPU/GPU throttling.
Chaos test: simulate regional network partition and validate spillover to nearest compatible region, measure tail-latency and failed fraction.
Canary verification: synthetic workload representing Tier-1 and Tier-3 customers with assertions on p99 and shed percentages.
